chunks: A number of our companions, from Abdullah al-Bazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), in a lengthy hadith:

Indeed, the first of all matters, its beginning, its strength, and its flourishing — without which nothing is of benefit — is the intellect, which God made an adornment for His creation and a light for them. So it is by the intellect that the servants recognized their Creator; that they are created beings, that He is the Regulator over them and they are the regulated ones, that He is the Eternal and they are the perishable. They reasoned by their intellects upon what they saw of His creation: His heavens and His earth, His sun and His moon, His night and His day — and that for Him and for them there is a Creator and a Regulator who has never ceased and will never cease. And they recognized by it the good from the ugly, that darkness lies in ignorance and that light lies in knowledge. So this is what the intellect indicated to them.

It was said to him: 'Can the servants then suffice themselves with the intellect alone, without anything else?' He said: 'The rational person, by the guidance of his intellect — which God made his straightener, his adornment, and his guidance — knows that God is the Truth and that He is his Lord. And he knows that for his Creator there is that which He loves and that which He dislikes, that there is obedience to Him and disobedience. Yet he does not find that his intellect alone can guide him to the specifics of all that. He knows that he cannot reach God except through knowledge and its seeking, and that he will not benefit from his intellect if he does not attain that through his knowledge. Thus it is obligatory upon the rational person to seek knowledge and the discipline without which there is no foundation.'

key_terms.الأدب: Adab — moral discipline, refinement, and proper conduct grounded in religious learning
key_terms.العقل: The intellect/reason — the God-given faculty that enables recognition of the Creator and moral discernment
key_terms.العلم: Knowledge — specifically revealed religious knowledge that the intellect alone cannot provide
key_terms.القوام: Foundation/support — that without which something cannot stand or function
key_terms.المدبر: The Regulator/Disposer — God as the One who manages and directs creation

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about the relationship between intellect and religious knowledge?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through a chain from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), addresses the relationship between intellect ('aql) and revealed knowledge ('ilm). The Imam explains that the intellect is God's gift of adornment and light to creation, enabling humans to recognize their Creator, distinguish good from evil, and understand that darkness is in ignorance while light is in knowledge. However, the intellect alone is insufficient — it leads the rational person to recognize that there must be divine commandments and prohibitions, yet cannot specify them on its own. Therefore, seeking religious knowledge ('ilm) and moral discipline (adab) becomes obligatory upon every rational being. The historical audience of early Muslim scholars would have recognized this as a response to debates between rationalists who elevated reason above revelation.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Abdullah Al Bazzaz, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Rahman Bin Hammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, in a lengthy Hadeeth: ‘The first of the matters, and its beginning, and its strengthening, and its building, which nothing is of benefit except with it, is the intellect, which Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Made it to be an adornment for His<sup>azwj</sup> creatures, and a light for them.

Thus, it is by the intellect that the servants recognise their Creator and that they are the created beings, and that He<sup>azwj</sup> is the Regulator for them and that they are the regulated ones, and that He<sup>azwj</sup> is the Eternal Being and there are the perishable beings, and they are indicated by their intellects upon what they are seeing from His<sup>azwj</sup> Creation, from His<sup>azwj</sup> sky, and His<sup>azwj</sup> earth, and His<sup>azwj</sup> sun, and His<sup>azwj</sup> moon, and His<sup>azwj</sup> night, and His<sup>azwj</sup> day, and that from him, and for them, there is a Creator and a Regulator, who has neither cease to be and will never cease to be. And they are recognising by it, the good from the ugly, and the darkness in the ignorance and the light in the knowledge. So this is what the intellect indicates them upon.

It was said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘So would the servants suffice themselves with the intellect besides other (things)?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The intellectual, due to the indication of his intellect which Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Made it to be his straightener, and his adornment, and his guidance, knows that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is He<sup>azwj</sup> Who is the Truth and that He<sup>azwj</sup> is his Lord<sup>azwj</sup>; and he knows that for his Creator there is Love and that for Him<sup>azwj</sup> is Dislikes, and that for Him<sup>azwj</sup> is obedience and that for him there is disobedience. 
So he would not find (except) for his intellect to indicate him upon that, and know that he cannot arrive to Him<sup>azwj</sup> except by the knowledge and its seeking, and that he would not benefit by his intellect if he does not attain that with his knowledge. Thus it is Obligatory upon the intellectual that he seeks the knowledge and the discipline which there is no foundation for him except by it’.
